items.title: Every bivariant class commutes with the class of a virtual normal sheaf
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For X locally of finite type over (S, delta), a closed subscheme Z with virtual normal sheaf N, a morphism Y -> X locally of finite type and c in A^*(Y -> X), the lemma asserts that c and c(Z -> X, N) commute in the sense of Remark labelled remark-bivariant-commute (statement lines 12205-12212). The proof uses Lemma labelled lemma-bivariant-zero to reduce to X integral, where the assertion becomes c cap c(Z -> X, N) cap [X] = c(Z -> X, N) cap c cap [X] in CH_*(Z x_X Y) (proof lines 12214-12221). Two cases follow. If Z = X then c(Z -> X, N) = c_top(N) by Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-fundamental, and Chern classes commute with any bivariant class by Lemma labelled lemma-cap-commutative-chern (proof lines 12223-12228). Otherwise Lemma labelled lemma-bivariant-zero allows a further reduction after blowing X up in a nonzero ideal, and blowing up in the ideal sheaf of Z brings one to the case where Z is an effective Cartier divisor by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor (proof lines 12230-12236). In that case c(Z -> X, N) = c_top(E) o i^* with i^* the Gysin homomorphism of the divisor and E the dual of the kernel of N^vee -> C_{Z/X} by Lemmas labelled lemma-gysin-decompose and lemma-gysin-agrees, and the claim follows because Chern classes are central in the bivariant ring in the strong sense of Lemma labelled lemma-cap-commutative-chern and c commutes with the Gysin homomorphism by the definition of bivariant classes (proof lines 12238-12248). The two step reduction, first to an integral base and then to a Cartier divisor after a blowup, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
